host.notes: First serious local Phase-2 integrated playtest.

unreal_cpp_build.notes: EverwardEditor Win64 Development build completed successfully via Unreal Engine 5.8 Build.bat.

probe_spawn.notes: EV-0001 spawned successfully in the Phase-2 runtime environment.

test_environment_visible.notes: Runtime-generated test environment and visible scan target were present and usable.

camera_orbit_zoom.notes: Mouse orbit and wheel zoom worked. Camera control is presentation-only; probe attitude itself cannot yet yaw, pitch, or roll.

hud_system_discovery.notes: Propulsion, Sensors, Computation, and Thermal Control were discoverable with Tab and bracket selection. Selection worked but was visually weak and easy to miss.

movement_x.notes: Forward/back translation worked. Movement currently uses world-space axes rather than probe-relative orientation.

stop_command.notes: Full stop worked well and materially improved navigation with intentionally clunky Generation-1 handling.

power_allocation.notes: Power could be increased/decreased across all four systems. Player requested persistent live watts/status beside every subsystem because current per-selection visibility obscures the whole allocation.

scan_complete.notes: Sensor scan could be started and allowed to complete successfully.

scan_cancel.notes: A second sensor scan could be cancelled successfully and did not later complete.

policy_install_clear.notes: Basic Survival policy installed and cleared successfully.

policy_compute_gate.notes: Computation minimum-power gate behaved as expected: policy executor unavailable below 25 W and available at or above 25 W.

manual_automation_shared_state.notes: Attempted with Sensors, but the expected policy-driven zeroing was not observed conclusively. This may have been because the Basic Survival energy threshold was not active. Retest with an explicit trigger state and clearer automation feedback.

warnings: No probe yaw, pitch, or roll; current translation feels world-axis/on-rails rather than like spacecraft flight.
Sensors and Thermal Control accept power changes but the gameplay consequence of those changes is not yet perceptible enough.
Automation state and causes are poorly explained; player could not confidently tell when or why Basic Survival changed subsystem state.
Systems HUD should show live power allocation and status for every installed subsystem simultaneously.
Placeholder sphere limits embodiment and the usefulness of further feel testing.
playtest_notes: The engineering integration is substantially functional, but the One Probe experience is not yet compelling. Generation-1 clunkiness itself landed well (4/5), while embodiment (2/5), automation comprehension (1/5), and desire to continue (1/5) show the next pass must focus on inhabiting and understanding EV-0001 rather than adding unrelated systems. Highest-value next playable pass: authoritative attitude/orientation with yaw/pitch/roll, probe-relative movement while preserving full stop, persistent per-system power/status telemetry, explicit automation cause/effect feedback, stronger perceptible sensor/thermal power effects, and replacement of the sphere with a recognizable Prime Probe blockout including articulated manipulator arms.
evidence: User-confirmed successful local Unreal Engine 5.8 run on commit 7f9ea88b8e7857f44f80b2f2327fde758dd2ca1a.
User-confirmed XYZ translation, full stop, subsystem power allocation, scan completion/cancellation, policy install/clear, and computation power gating.
User subjective ratings captured during the same playtest session.
